newsitem.title: GERMANY: SOCCER-GERMANS PLAN TOP SECURITY FOR DORTMUND-UNITED TIE.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-GERMANS PLAN TOP SECURITY FOR DORTMUND-UNITED TIE.

text.p: Dortmund police will mount their tightest-ever security operation for a club soccer match when Manchester United visit the city on Wednesday -- but will still allow English and German fans to mingle in a street party before the match.

Police chief Bernhard Leidiger said on Monday that more officers would be on duty for the European Cup semifinal first leg than at any Dortmund match in the past. The Germans are expecting about 500 United fans to turn up without tickets.
"We never give out numbers of police involved but there will be more police than ever before at a match. We have intensified security," Leidiger said.
United fans were involved in trouble at the club's last away tie in Portugal. Eight English fans were injured after a clash with riot police at the quarter-final in Porto.
But Borussia Dortmund said they planned to go ahead with a party in the middle of the city on the day of the match which is aimed at bringing together fans from both clubs in a friendly atmosphere.
Around 4,000 English fans -- 3,400 have tickets -- are expected to travel to the city in the heart of the industrial Ruhr region.
"We have never had problems with parties like this before and we have had them since 1986. We hope the English fans are going to behave like good guests," Leidiger said.
"Our information is that there were organisational problems in Porto and it was not the English fans."
Dortmund, who do not have huge problems with hooliganism, hope to start the party at midday in the centre of the city.
A group of Dortmund fans will also greet United fans with banners welcoming them to the city when they arrive.

Asked if the club was not worried that it was setting up a stage for possible trouble, spokesman Josef Schneck said: "We have had this 15 times before at European games and it has been peaceful with clubs like (Glasgow) Celtic and Ajax Amsterdam.
"There is going to be music and bands from Manchester there. We hope we are going to have a peaceful party for fans."

Barry Moorhouse, membership secretary of Manchester United's Supporters' Club, welcomed the initiative. "It should be a carnival atmosphere," he said on Monday. "They're calling it a 'Fans' Project' with music, videos etc. We're taking some videos of United and some former players are also going along.
"I don't think there will be any problems."
The match will mark the first meeting of the two clubs in a European competition for more than 30 years.
